entries.head: narrow down

senses.en: to reduce the number of choices

example.en: We narrowed it down to two apartments.
example.zh: 我们筛到只剩两套公寓。

entries.l1_note: 缩小范围是 narrow down；narrow 单独是窄的。

entries.head: decide against

senses.en: to choose not to do something

example.en: We decided against the bigger apartment.
example.zh: 我们决定不要那套大公寓了。

entries.l1_note: 决定不做是 decide against；decide on 是选定。

entries.head: go through with

senses.en: to do something you planned despite doubts

example.en: She went through with the move despite the cost.
example.zh: 虽然贵她还是搬了。

entries.l1_note: 做到底是 go through with；go through 是经历。

entries.head: come down to

senses.en: when the real issue is one thing

example.en: It comes down to whether we can afford it.
example.zh: 说到底就是我们买不买得起。

entries.l1_note: 归结为是 come down to；boil down to 同义。

entries.head: size up

senses.en: to look at something and judge it

example.en: She sized up the room before choosing a seat.
example.zh: 她扫了一眼房间才挑座位。

entries.l1_note: 打量是 size up；不是“量尺寸”。

example.en: Consider the offer before you say no.
example.zh: 拒绝前先考虑一下这个 offer。

entries.head: toss around

example.en: We tossed around a few names for the project.
example.zh: 我们随便聊了几个项目名。

entries.l1_note: 随便讨论是 toss around；toss out 是扔掉。

entries.head: bat around

senses.en: to discuss an idea from several angles

example.en: They batted the proposal around for an hour.
example.zh: 他们把提案来回讨论了一小时。

entries.l1_note: bat around 来自棒球，画面是互相打来打去。

example.en: We settled the details over lunch.
example.zh: 午饭时我们把细节敲定了。

entries.head: hit on

senses.en: to suddenly think of an idea

example.en: She hit on a much cheaper solution.
example.zh: 她突然想到一个便宜得多的办法。

entries.l1_note: 突然想到是 hit on；hit on someone 是搭讪。

entries.head: jump at

example.en: I jumped at the chance to work abroad.
example.zh: 我立刻抓住了出国的机会。

entries.l1_note: 立刻接受是 jump at；jump in 是插话。

entries.head: leap at

example.en: She leapt at the chance to lead the team.
example.zh: 她立刻接下了带团队的机会。

entries.l1_note: leap at 和 jump at 同义，稍书面。

entries.head: pass up

example.en: He passed up a job in Shenzhen to stay home.
example.zh: 他放弃了深圳的工作留在家里。

entries.l1_note: 放弃机会是 pass up；pass on 是转达。

entries.head: win over

senses.en: to get someone to support you

example.en: She won over the skeptics with a demo.
example.zh: 她用一次演示说服了持怀疑的人。

entries.l1_note: 争取过来是 win over；win out 是最终胜出。

entries.head: scare off

example.en: The high price scared off most buyers.
example.zh: 高价吓跑了大部分买家。

entries.l1_note: 吓跑是 scare off / scare away。

entries.head: sit on

example.en: You can't sit on this request all week.
example.zh: 这个申请你不能压一周。

entries.l1_note: 压着是 sit on；sit in 是旁听。

entries.head: put on hold

example.en: The trip is on hold until the budget clears.
example.zh: 预算批下来之前旅行先搁着。

entries.l1_note: 搁置是 put on hold；hold on 是别挂电话。

entries.head: think ahead

example.en: Think ahead — where do you want to be in five years?
example.zh: 往前想想，五年后你想在哪？

entries.l1_note: 提前想是 think ahead；think back 是回想。

entries.head: look ahead

senses.en: to consider what will happen next

example.en: Looking ahead, the schedule gets tight in May.
example.zh: 往后看，五月的日程会很紧。

entries.l1_note: 往前看是 look ahead；look back 是回顾。

entries.head: plan ahead

example.en: Plan ahead if you want cheap tickets.
example.zh: 想买便宜票就得提前计划。

entries.l1_note: 提前计划是 plan ahead；plan out 是排细节。

entries.head: rule in

example.en: We can't rule in the cheaper plan until we test it.
example.zh: 便宜方案没测过之前不能算进来。

entries.l1_note: 纳入考虑是 rule in；rule out 是排除。

entries.head: factor in

senses.en: to include something in your planning

example.en: Factor in the commute before you take the job.
example.zh: 接这份工作前把通勤算进去。

entries.l1_note: 算进去是 factor in；factor 是因素。

entries.head: weigh against

senses.en: to compare one thing with another

example.en: Weigh the salary against the hours you'll work.
example.zh: 把工资和工作时长放一起比。

entries.l1_note: 权衡是 weigh A against B；weigh up 是整体权衡。
collocations: weigh the pros against the cons

entries.head: trade off

senses.en: to accept a disadvantage to get an advantage

example.en: You trade off space for a shorter commute here.
example.zh: 在这儿是用面积换更短的通勤。

entries.l1_note: 取舍是 trade off；名词是 trade-off。

entries.head: balance out

senses.en: when advantages and disadvantages cancel out

example.en: The extra pay balances out the longer hours.
example.zh: 多给的工资抵得上多干的时间。

entries.l1_note: 扯平是 balance out；balance 是平衡。

entries.head: think back

example.en: Think back to when you first moved here.
example.zh: 回想你刚搬来的时候。

entries.l1_note: 回想是 think back (to)；think ahead 是往前想。

entries.head: look back

example.en: Looking back, I should have taken the offer.
example.zh: 回头看，我当时该接那个 offer。

entries.l1_note: 回顾是 look back (on)；look ahead 是往前看。

example.en: Let's discuss the budget tomorrow.
example.zh: 我们明天讨论预算。

entries.head: kick around

example.en: We kicked around the idea of a podcast.
example.zh: 我们随便聊了聊做播客的想法。

entries.l1_note: 随便聊是 kick around；kick off 是启动。

entries.head: play with

senses.en: to consider an idea without deciding

example.en: I'm playing with the idea of moving back.
example.zh: 我在考虑搬回去这件事。

entries.l1_note: 考虑想法是 play with the idea；play around 是瞎试。

entries.head: occur to

senses.en: if an idea occurs to you, you suddenly think of it

example.en: It occurred to me that we never booked the hotel.
example.zh: 我突然想到我们根本没订酒店。

entries.l1_note: occur to someone；主语是想法，不是人。不说 I occurred to an idea。

entries.head: bring about

example.en: The new policy brought about a big change in hiring.
example.zh: 新政策让招聘发生了很大变化。

entries.l1_note: bring about + 变化/结果；不是“带过来”。

entries.head: come about

example.en: How did this mix-up come about?
example.zh: 这个乌龙是怎么发生的？

entries.l1_note: come about 是不及物，常问 how something came about。

entries.head: go about

senses.en: to start dealing with a task in a particular way

example.en: She went about the complaint calmly and got a refund.
example.zh: 她冷静地处理投诉，拿到了退款。

entries.l1_note: go about + 事情；不是“到处走”。
collocations: go about it the right way

entries.head: go along with

senses.en: to agree with a plan or person

example.en: I'll go along with the new schedule if everyone else agrees.
example.zh: 大家都同意的话，我也接受新排期。

entries.l1_note: go along with + 人/计划；不是“和……一起走”。

entries.head: lead up to

senses.en: to cause or prepare for an event

example.en: The small delays led up to a missed flight.
example.zh: 一次次小延误最后导致错过了航班。

entries.l1_note: lead up to + 事件；不是“带上去”。
collocations: the events leading up to it

entries.head: stand for

example.en: The letters HR stand for human resources.
example.zh: HR 这两个字母代表人力资源。

example.en: I won't stand for that kind of language.
example.zh: 那种话我不会容忍。

entries.l1_note: 代表义常用缩写作主语；容忍义多用于否定句。

entries.head: think of

senses.en: to have an idea or suggestion

example.en: Can you think of a cheaper way to get there?
example.zh: 你能想到更便宜的走法吗？

example.en: I can't think of her name right now.
example.zh: 我一时想不起她叫什么。

entries.l1_note: think of 是“想到/想起”；think about 是“考虑”。

example.en: Pay close attention to the contract details.
example.zh: 仔细注意合同细节。

entries.head: think big

example.en: If we want to grow, we need to think big.
example.zh: 想增长就得往大处想。

entries.l1_note: think big 是“往大处想”；反义是 think small。

entries.head: up in the air

example.en: The launch date is still up in the air.
example.zh: 发布时间还没定。

entries.l1_note: up in the air 是“悬而未决”；不是“在空中”。
collocations: leave it up in the air

entries.head: time's up

example.en: Time's up — please put your pens down.
example.zh: 时间到，请停笔。

entries.l1_note: time's up 是“时间到”；不是“时间上去了”。

entries.head: act on

example.en: We need to act on the client's feedback today.
example.zh: 我们今天得按客户的反馈行动。

entries.l1_note: act on + 建议/信息；不是 act for。

entries.head: advise against

example.en: The doctor advised against running for a week.
example.zh: 医生建议一周内不要跑步。

entries.l1_note: advise against doing 是建议别做；advise to do 是建议做。

entries.head: allow for

example.en: Allow for extra time at the airport.
example.zh: 在机场要留出额外时间。

entries.l1_note: allow for 是考虑到/留出；allow 单独用是允许。

entries.head: base on

example.en: We based the plan on last year's data.
example.zh: 我们根据去年的数据定了这个计划。

entries.l1_note: base A on B；被动是 be based on。

entries.head: come after

example.en: The refund will come after the inspection.
example.zh: 退款会在检查之后到。

entries.l1_note: come after 是时间/顺序在后；不是“追着来”。

entries.head: decide on

example.en: We decided on the blue design.
example.zh: 我们选定了蓝色那款。

entries.l1_note: decide on + 选项；decide to do 是决定做。

entries.head: depend on

example.en: The launch depends on the final test.
example.zh: 发布取决于最后一轮测试。

entries.l1_note: depend on + 人/事；不是 depend of。

example.en: Don't let one failure discourage you.
example.zh: 别因为一次失败就泄气。

entries.head: do something about

example.en: We need to do something about the noise.
example.zh: 我们得想办法处理噪音。

entries.l1_note: do something about + 问题；不是“对……做某事”。

entries.head: hinge on

example.en: The whole plan hinges on the bank loan.
example.zh: 整个计划取决于银行贷款。

entries.l1_note: hinge on/upon + 关键因素；不是“铰链”。

entries.head: insist on

example.en: She insisted on paying for dinner.
example.zh: 她坚持要付晚饭钱。

entries.l1_note: insist on + 名词/doing；不是 insist to。

entries.head: leave up to

example.en: We'll leave the final choice up to you.
example.zh: 最后的选择交给你。

entries.l1_note: leave something up to someone；代词放 up 前。

entries.head: look at

example.en: Let's look at the numbers again.
example.zh: 我们再看看数字。

entries.l1_note: look at 可指看，也可指考虑/看待。

entries.head: look to

example.en: We look to the manager for a decision.
example.zh: 我们指望经理做决定。

entries.l1_note: look to someone for something；不是“看向”。

entries.head: plan for

example.en: We're planning for a busy fall.
example.zh: 我们在为忙碌的秋天做计划。

entries.l1_note: plan for + 情况/时间；plan to do 是计划做。

entries.head: play on

example.en: The ad plays on people's fear of missing out.
example.zh: 这则广告利用了人们怕错过的心理。

entries.l1_note: play on + 情绪/弱点；不是“玩”。

entries.head: reflect on

example.en: Take a day to reflect on what went wrong.
example.zh: 花一天反思哪里出了问题。

entries.l1_note: reflect on + 事情；不是“反射”。

entries.head: rely on

example.en: We rely on the subway to get to work.
example.zh: 我们靠地铁上班。

entries.l1_note: rely on + 人/事；不是 rely in。

entries.head: result from

example.en: The delay resulted from a missing document.
example.zh: 延误是因为少了一份文件。

entries.l1_note: result from + 原因；result in + 结果。

entries.head: result in

example.en: The mistake resulted in a big refund.
example.zh: 这个错误导致了一大笔退款。

entries.l1_note: result in + 结果；result from + 原因。

entries.head: rush into

example.en: Don't rush into buying a car.
example.zh: 别急着买车。

entries.l1_note: rush into + 决定/行动；不是“冲进去”的字面义。

entries.head: stem from

example.en: The problem stems from unclear instructions.
example.zh: 问题源于指令不清楚。

entries.l1_note: stem from + 原因；不是“茎”。

entries.head: become of

example.en: What became of the old coffee shop?
example.zh: 那家老咖啡店后来怎么样了？

entries.l1_note: what became of...? 是“后来怎么样了”；不是“成为”。

entries.head: call for

example.en: This situation calls for a calm response.
example.zh: 这种情况需要冷静回应。

entries.l1_note: call for + 需要/要求；不是“打电话找”。

entries.head: come out of

example.en: The idea came out of a casual lunch chat.
example.zh: 这个想法来自一次午饭闲聊。

entries.l1_note: come out of + 来源；不是“从……出来”的字面义。

entries.head: figure on

example.en: I figured on spending about two hours there.
example.zh: 我预计在那儿待两个小时左右。

entries.l1_note: figure on + 预计的事；不是“算在……上”。

entries.head: push for

example.en: The staff are pushing for a four-day week.
example.zh: 员工在争取四天工作制。

entries.l1_note: push for + 目标；不是“推”。

entries.head: resort to

example.en: We had to resort to a backup plan.
example.zh: 我们不得不动用备用方案。

entries.l1_note: resort to + 办法；常带“没办法才用”的意思。

entries.head: think outside the box

example.en: We need to think outside the box on pricing.
example.zh: 定价上我们得跳出框框想。

entries.l1_note: think outside the box 是创新思考；不是“在盒子外想”。

example.en: In the future, I want to work from home more.
example.zh: 以后我想多在家办公。

example.en: In ten years, this area will have two more subway lines.
example.zh: 十年后这一片会多两条地铁。

example.en: Sooner or later, you'll have to tell your parents.
example.zh: 迟早你得告诉你爸妈。

example.en: One of these days I'll clean out the closet.
example.zh: 总有一天我要把衣柜清理了。

example.en: The food will be ready in no time.
example.zh: 饭很快就好。

example.en: The weekend will be over before you know it.
example.zh: 不知不觉周末就过完了。

example.en: I bet it will rain before we get there.
example.zh: 我敢打赌我们到之前会下雨。

example.en: Mark my words, he'll be a manager in two years.
example.zh: 记住我的话，他两年内会当经理。

example.en: Time will tell if the new plan works.
example.zh: 新计划行不行，时间会证明。

example.en: Don't give up; things will get better.
example.zh: 别放弃，一切会好起来的。

example.en: I guess we should leave now.
example.zh: 我猜我们该走了。

example.en: I suppose you're right about the time.
example.zh: 关于时间，我想你是对的。

example.en: Is the meeting at three? I think so.
example.zh: 会议是三点吗？我想是的。

example.en: Will he come? I don't think so.
example.zh: 他会来吗？我不这么认为。

example.en: Will it rain? Maybe not.
example.zh: 会下雨吗？也许不会。

example.en: I would say it's about twenty minutes on foot.
example.zh: 我会说走路大概二十分钟。

example.en: It seems like everyone is busy this week.
example.zh: 看起来这周大家都很忙。

example.en: It sounds like a good deal.
example.zh: 听起来挺划算。

example.en: The work is more or less done.
example.zh: 工作差不多做完了。

example.en: I'm kind of tired tonight.
example.zh: 我今晚有点儿累。

example.en: I'm sure I locked the door.
example.zh: 我确定我锁门了。

example.en: He's coming for sure.
example.zh: 他肯定会来。

example.en: Of course you can bring a friend.
example.zh: 当然可以带朋友。

example.en: No doubt she'll get the job.
example.zh: 毫无疑问她会拿到这份工作。

example.en: There's no way we can finish by Friday.
example.zh: 我们不可能周五前做完。

example.en: I'm positive the package arrived today.
example.zh: 我十分确定包裹今天到了。

example.en: I know for a fact that the store is open.
example.zh: 我确定那家店开着。

example.en: Take my word for it; the noodles are worth the line.
example.zh: 相信我的话，这面值得排队。

example.en: I'll be there at eight; you can count on it.
example.zh: 我八点到，你尽管放心。

example.en: You bet I'll be at the party.
example.zh: 当然啦，我肯定去聚会。

example.en: I'm not sure which exit to take.
example.zh: 我不确定该走哪个出口。

example.en: I'm not one hundred percent sure about the date.
example.zh: 日期我没有百分百把握。

example.en: I have no idea where my keys are.
example.zh: 我完全不知道钥匙在哪。

example.en: Who knows when the rain will stop.
example.zh: 谁知道雨什么时候停。

example.en: It's hard to say who will win.
example.zh: 谁会赢很难说。

example.en: It depends on the weather.
example.zh: 看天气。

example.en: I can't say for sure until I check.
example.zh: 我查了才敢肯定。

entries.head: your guess is as good as mine

example.en: Where is he? Your guess is as good as mine.
example.zh: 他在哪？我也不知道。

example.en: I might be wrong, but I think it's closed.
example.zh: 我可能记错，但那家好像关门了。

example.en: You never know; he might say yes.
example.zh: 说不准，他也许会答应。

example.en: There's a good chance it will snow tonight.
example.zh: 今晚很有可能下雪。

example.en: Chances are the train will be crowded.
example.zh: 地铁多半会很挤。

example.en: It's possible to finish today if we hurry.
example.zh: 抓紧的话今天有可能做完。

example.en: The match could go either way.
example.zh: 这场比赛两种结果都有可能。

example.en: It's likely that the meeting will run late.
example.zh: 会议很可能开得晚。

example.en: With any luck, we'll get there by noon.
example.zh: 运气好的话，我们中午能到。

example.en: If all goes well, we'll move in next month.
example.zh: 一切顺利的话，我们下个月搬进去。

example.en: In a final like this, anything can happen.
example.zh: 这样的决赛，一切皆有可能。

example.en: I know it sounds crazy, but it just might work.
example.zh: 我知道听着离谱，但也许能行。

example.en: He says he'll be on time. I doubt it.
example.zh: 他说会准时。我怀疑。

example.en: That excuse? I don't buy it.
example.zh: 那个借口？我才不信。

entries.head: I find that hard to believe

example.en: I find that hard to believe.
example.zh: 我很难相信。

example.en: The numbers don't match; nothing adds up.
example.zh: 数字对不上，完全说不通。

example.en: You say you fixed it? Prove it.
example.zh: 你说修好了？拿出证据来。

example.en: Something sounds fishy about that offer.
example.zh: 那个报价听着不对劲。

entries.head: I'll believe it when I see it

example.en: I'll believe it when I see it.
example.zh: 眼见为实。

example.en: You must be joking; the price is double.
example.zh: 你在开玩笑吧，价格翻倍了。

entries.head: I would not be so sure

example.en: I wouldn't be so sure about the weather.
example.zh: 天气我可没那么肯定。

example.en: That doesn't sound right; check the address again.
example.zh: 听着不太对，再核对一下地址。

example.en: Trust me; this shortcut saves ten minutes.
example.zh: 相信我，这条近路能省十分钟。

example.en: I believe you; it wasn't your fault.
example.zh: 我相信你，不是你的错。

example.en: Believe it or not, he finished in one day.
example.zh: 信不信由你，他一天就做完了。

example.en: I knew it; the key was in your pocket.
example.zh: 我就知道，钥匙在你口袋里。

example.en: The coach has faith in the young players.
example.zh: 教练信任年轻球员。

example.en: It's going to be a long week, that's for sure.
example.zh: 这一周会很长，那肯定的。

example.en: I told you so; the store closes at eight.
example.zh: 我早说过，这家店八点关门。

example.en: I'm convinced; let's go with your plan.
example.zh: 我信了，就按你的计划来。

example.en: I have no doubt she'll pass the exam.
example.zh: 我毫不怀疑她会通过考试。

example.en: Be sure of the address before you order.
example.zh: 下单前确认好地址。

example.en: We made plans for the long weekend.
example.zh: 我们为长周末做了计划。

example.en: Pick a day that works for everyone.
example.zh: 挑个大家都方便的日子。

example.en: Clear your schedule for Thursday afternoon.
example.zh: 周四下午把日程空出来。

example.en: Put the deadline on the calendar.
example.zh: 把截止日期记到日历上。

example.en: We'll figure out the details later.
example.zh: 细节我们回头再商量。

example.en: Keep Saturday free for the game.
example.zh: 周六留出空档看比赛。

example.en: Dinner at seven? Sounds like a plan.
example.zh: 七点吃饭？就这么办。

example.en: We'll play it by ear depending on the weather.
example.zh: 看天气再说。

example.en: I'll pencil you in for Tuesday morning.
example.zh: 我先把你记在周二上午。

example.en: I can't make up my mind between the two.
example.zh: 这两个我下不了决心。

example.en: We need to make a decision by Friday.
example.zh: 周五前我们得做出决定。

example.en: We decided on the blue one.
example.zh: 我们选定了蓝色的。

example.en: Two hundred? It's a deal.
example.zh: 两百？成交。

example.en: Let's flip a coin to decide.
example.zh: 抛硬币决定吧。

example.en: I'll go for the smaller apartment.
example.zh: 我倾向于选小一点的公寓。

example.en: Think it over and call me tomorrow.
example.zh: 再想想，明天打给我。

example.en: On second thought, let's take the train.
example.zh: 转念一想，我们坐火车吧。

example.en: There are three colors; take your pick.
example.zh: 有三个颜色，随便挑。

example.en: She had a change of heart and said yes.
example.zh: 她改了主意，答应了。
